The test merged in #11637 imported `getTestDbConfig` from
`^/test/setup/mongo/utils`, which does not export it — the symbol lives in
`./test-db-config`. That broke `lint:typecheck` (TS2305) and made the suite
fail at runtime (`getTestDbConfig is not a function`). #11637 was merged
without ci-app-lint / ci-app-test-integration having run on it.

opened, matching the two sibling migration integ tests. No second MongoClient
and no dependency on how the per-worker database name is resolved.

Two further problems the same file had:

- Both `up()` and `down()` operate on the whole database, and `down()` rewrites
  every pageId-keyed revision back to the legacy path-keyed shape. Sharing a
  database with the ordinary integration tests lets it corrupt fixtures another
  file in the same worker left behind, so the file moves to the
  `app-integration-exclusive` project (`*.exclusive.integ.ts`), which gets a
  database name no other project's worker is given.

- The migration unconditionally called `mongoose.connect(getMongoUri())`.
  `getMongoUri()` reads MONGO_URI, which in CI names the base database while
  mongoose is bound to the per-worker one, so the second connect threw
  "Can't call `openUri()` on an active connection with different connection
  strings" and every test failed. It now connects only when disconnected —
  unchanged under the migrate-mongo CLI, which opens no connection of its own.

test(growi-vault): stop the reconcile overhead test failing in pairs

This file failed twice in one CI run (run 31175665930) and the two failures
were one defect:

    × accept gate resolves within 200ms ... → expected 313 to be less than 200
    × vault_instructions count equals N ... → expected 26 to be 25

The second is caused by the first. Each test waits for its background reconcile
to reach a terminal state at the END of the test body, so an assertion that
fails before that wait skips it. `afterEach` then empties vault_instructions
while the reconcile is still writing, and the late row is counted by the next
test.

Two changes:

- `afterEach` now drains any in-flight reconcile before deleting, so cleanup no
  longer depends on the test having passed. Forcing the accept-gate test to fail
  used to turn the next test into "expected 26 to be 25"; now it fails alone.

- The accept-gate test asserts the contract relatively — submit returns while
  the reconcile it scheduled is still in flight — instead of `elapsed < 200ms`.
  The absolute bound was wrong in both directions. It failed on runner noise
  alone (313ms on an otherwise healthy run), and it could not catch the
  regression it looked like it guarded: measured locally the gate takes ~8ms and
  the entire reconcile ~63ms, so a gate that awaited the whole reconcile would
  still have passed under 200ms. Asserting it relatively is immune to how loaded
  the runner is, because a slower machine slows both sides together.

要件 6.10's "accept gate p99 <= 200ms" is a production SLO; a single sample in
CI cannot measure a p99, and this test no longer pretends to.

Verified: forced-failure run shows no cascade, 5 consecutive clean runs, and the
reconcile suite (11 tests) passes.

fix: Delete the redirect for a path before creating a page there

A page created at a path that still carries a redirect is unreachable at its own
path: page view resolves a requested path through its redirect
(resolvePathAndCheckIdentical) without ever looking for a live page at it. The
delete that prevents this ran in createSubOperation, which create() does not
await and which logged a deleteOne failure without acting on it — so one
transient failure left that state permanently, and even the ordinary path left
it in place for as long as the sub operation took to reach the delete.

Move the delete into create(), after validation and before anything is written,
and let a failure abort the creation. Deleting first is what makes the failure
safe: the redirect is still in place and no page was created, so the operation
is retryable — whereas deleting after the save would leave exactly the state
this is meant to prevent, with no way to undo it. The log line now fires only
when a redirect was actually deleted, instead of warning on every create.

fix(pages): make the delete conflict check able to fire

POST /_api/v3/pages/delete filters the selected pages through
`p.isUpdatable(pageIdToRevisionIdMap[p._id])`, but `isUpdatable` is async
(models/obsolete-page.js), so the predicate was a Promise — always truthy. The
filter therefore removed nothing and a page was soft deleted even when the
revisionId the client had seen was no longer the latest.

`Array#filter` cannot await, so the flags are resolved with `Promise.all` first and
the filter reads them by index. The `p.isEmpty` short circuit is kept: an empty page
has no revision to compare, and only a non-empty page reads its entry out of
`pageIdToRevisionIdMap`.

The lookup is wrapped in try/catch because awaiting it makes two failures reachable
that were silently swallowed before: a rejected `isUpdatable` (its `populate` throws
for a page whose revision is missing) and a `pageIdToRevisionIdMap` entry that is not
set. Without the catch either one would leave the request hanging.

The added integration test is RED without this change: the page with a stale
revisionId is deleted and the route answers 200 instead of refusing.

The refusal is reported as `500 No pages can be deleted.`, which is what the route
already did when every selected page was filtered out. Answering 409 for a conflict
would be an improvement, but it changes the contract, so it is left as it is here and
the test records the current status.

fix: Links to pages with non-ASCII paths reload the whole document

NextLink decides whether a link can use client-side routing by passing
`URL.pathname` to `isCreatablePage()`. `URL.pathname` is percent-encoded,
and '%' is one of the characters `isCreatablePage()` forbids, so every
path holding a non-ASCII character or a space was judged non-creatable
and fell back to a plain anchor -- reloading the whole document.

Decode the pathname before the check. The change is one-directional:
a pathname without '%' decodes to itself, and one with '%' was already
rejected, so no link that used client-side routing can lose it.

fix(rate-limiter): test the rate-limit boundary directly instead of looping to it

The maxRequest:500/random tests issued up to maxRequests+1 sequential
consumePoints() round-trips to Mongo just to reach the boundary, which made
their wall time scale with maxRequests and therefore sensitive to CI runner
load contention (#11718) — bumping the timeout only buys headroom until CI
gets busier again.

Seed the counter to maxRequests-1 with a single penalty() call (same Mongo
upsert path consume() uses) and exercise only the two boundary-crossing
calls through the real consumePoints() wrapper. This cuts the round-trip
count from up to 501 to 3 per test, removing the scaling behavior rather
than padding around it.

Keep a modest explicit timeout (8s, versus the prior 15s) since local
devcontainer timing and the GitHub Actions runner are not the same
environment and we don't yet have CI history for this shape.

fix(tags-input): stabilize typeahead search callback to stop dropped searches

TagsInput's searchHandler (passed as AsyncTypeahead's onSearch) depended on
tagsSearch?.tags, so its identity changed whenever the SWR search request
resolved. react-bootstrap-typeahead's useAsync recreates its internal
debounced search function whenever onSearch's identity changes, and its
effect cleanup cancels any pending debounced call. When the modal's initial
/tags.search?q='' request resolved while a just-typed keystroke's 200ms
debounce was still pending, that pending search was silently cancelled and
never re-fired — the typeahead dropdown item never rendered.

Read the latest search results through a ref instead, so searchHandler has a
stable identity across renders. Also stop mutating the SWR cache's tags
array via unshift(); build a new array instead.

fix(playwright): stabilize flaky emacs-keymap bold/link tests

The Emacs keymap CodeMirror extension attaches via an async dynamic
import (getKeymap -> emacsKeymap -> @replit/codemirror-emacs) that
resolves after the editor is already visible and interactive. Until
it resolves the default CodeMirror keymap is still active, so a
keystroke sent in that window types as literal characters instead of
firing the Emacs binding. Retry the bold and link interactions
(resetting editor content first) until they observably succeed,
following the same expect(...).toPass() pattern already used for the
identical shortcut-attach race in saving.spec.ts.

fix(app-test): stabilize flaky delete-pages.integ.ts — wait for full background delete chain

The route fires deleteMultiplePages without awaiting it, and deletePage moves
the target to trash before it awaits updateDescendantCountOfAncestors on the
parent. Waiting only for the target's own status flip let afterEach's fixture
cleanup delete that parent before the still-in-flight count update looked it
up, throwing an unhandled "Target not found" rejection.

Fixes #11740

fix(app-test): give the delete-pages race-fix test a longer timeout

The first PR-CI run showed the two sequential 10s-cap polling waits
exceeding vitest's 5s default under load (Test timed out in 5000ms),
not the original race — the fix itself worked (all 920 named tests
passed, no unhandled rejection).

fix(app-test): wait for ancestor removal, not descendantCount, in delete-pages race fix

The previous commit's wait condition (poll for the parent's descendantCount
to decrement) was itself unreliable: trashing the target clears its own
`parent` field, so once the count update finishes, the very next awaited
step in the same chain (removeLeafEmptyPagesRecursively) finds the now-
childless fixture-root ancestor and deletes it within the same tick — a
window a 50ms poll can't reliably observe, confirmed by CI (the wait timed
out deterministically). The ancestor's removal is the chain's last mutation
and a stable terminal state, unlike the transient count change, so waiting
for that instead reliably proves the whole chain has settled.

fix(growi-vault): remove flaky race in reconcile-flow completed-audit wait

reconcile-flow.integ.ts scenario (b) polled the DB for status "completed"
then slept a fixed 100ms before asserting on the audit events array. The
orchestrator emits the "completed" audit event strictly after the DB write,
so under CI load the fixed sleep isn't always enough time for that emit to
land before the assertion runs. Replace the sleep with a poll that waits
for the actual audit event, mirroring the existing waitForReconcileStatus
helper.

fix(page): harden the expired WIP page sweep after code review

Make the claim non-destructive. It was findOneAndDelete, so the page row
disappeared strictly before the cascade that removes its revisions,
attachments and search-index entries — any failure or crash in between left
that data orphaned with nothing in the collection able to select the page for
a retry. The claim now withdraws wipExpiredAt via findOneAndUpdate instead:
still exactly-once (the filter requires the expiry to be set), but the page
document is removed only by deleteCompletelyOperation, together with
everything belonging to it. A failed deletion now leaves the page intact, so
the summary's `failed` means what it says.

Re-check for children by parent link after claiming. Page creation inserts
the child and updates its ancestors' counts in separate operations, so a page
that has just gained a child still reads descendantCount 0 and passes both
the sweep filter and the claim — deleting it orphaned the child. Aborting
leaves the page alive without an expiry, which is the invariant's own target
state. The residual window (a child inserted during the deletion itself) is
documented rather than papered over.

Other review fixes:

- Remove a stray unused `dotenv-flow` import from the page service.
- Declare the wipExpiredAt index sparse (only WIP pages carry the field, and
  a `$lte: Date` query never matches null), and drop-then-create it in the
  migration so an existing index with different options cannot make mongoose's
  autoIndex fail with IndexOptionsConflict on every boot.
- Declare makeWip/publish/unpublish on PageDocument: the `[x: string]: any`
  index signature let makeWip's new required parameter be omitted silently,
  storing `new Date(NaN)`.
- Move the cleanup cron schedule to app:wipPageCleanupCronSchedule
  (WIP_PAGE_CLEANUP_CRON_SCHEDULE, empty disables) so an operator can move or
  turn off a collection-wide sweep, with a spec for the gate.
- Reject overlapping page tree repair runs; the admin UI's disabled button is
  per-browser and resets on reload.
- Use ~/utils/logger in the new files (it owns initializeLoggerFactory;
  importing @growi/logger directly loses the app's log-level config if it
  loads first), and give the extracted module its own namespace.
- Update prisma/schema.prisma for the renamed field and index.
- Add the changeset for the breaking @growi/core IPage rename.
- Project and .lean() the sweep cursor, which only needs three fields.

fix(page): stop the WIP sweep from mass-deleting on upgrade, and retry failures

Two data-loss blockers found in code review of the TTL -> cron migration.

1. The migration could hand out already-expired values. Adding the expiration
   window to `ttlTimestamp` is not enough on its own: a timestamp older than one
   window still converts to a past instant, which is the normal state on an
   instance whose TTL monitor was not reaping. The first sweep after the upgrade
   would then delete that whole backlog completely -- revisions, attachments and
   search-index entries included, with no trash to restore from. Anything already
   overdue is now re-granted a full window from the migration instead, and the
   count is logged so operators can act before it arrives.

2. A page whose deletion threw was never retried. The claim withdraws
   `wipExpiredAt` before deleting, and the sweep selects on that field, so a
   transient failure dropped the page out of every future sweep with only a log
   line to show for it. The expiry is now re-armed with a short backoff, filtered
   so a page that was published, re-claimed or removed meanwhile is left alone.

   For that retry to be safe, deletePageCompletelyBySystem now runs
   deleteCompletelyOperation BEFORE the ancestor decrement: otherwise every retry
   would subtract from the ancestors again and permanently understate
   descendantCount. This also removes a pre-existing corruption, where any
   failure left ancestors decremented for a page that still existed.

The migration test asserting "the page is not already expired" checked only
`> madeWipAt`, and its fixture had aged into the overdue branch, so it never
verified its own claim. Fixtures are now relative to now, and the branch is
pinned from both sides.

fix(page): bound the page tree repair and cover its data-loss guards

Addresses the "should fix" findings from the PR review.

Scale (#3): the empty-page sweep materialised every orphan into one `$in`, which
breaches the 16 MB BSON limit on a large backlog, and re-scanned the whole
collection once per cascade level. Both copies (the boot migration and the admin
service) now work in bounded batches, and passes after the first only re-examine
the parents of what was just deleted — nothing else can have become a childless
placeholder as a result of the run. The migration's conversion queries are
chunked for the same reason.

Guards without tests (#4): the route's maintenance-mode gate and its

argument — a stale snapshot is exactly the race, so the test reproduces it by
passing one rather than by interleaving.

The cron also ignored maintenance mode, so it could delete pages while the repair
was recounting descendantCount over them. It now stands down; the pages stay
expired and the next run collects them.

Dead code (#5): dropped the unused re-export from the repair-page-tree barrel.

Off-tree pages (#6): `recountAllDescendantCounts` lacked `addConditionAsOnTree()`,

fix(page): keep the WIP expiry migration to the schema and value change

Drop the empty-page cleanup from the migration and stream the conversion, so
up() does the field/index migration and nothing else.

Cleanup is no longer the migration's job: pages the cron deletes are cleaned up
in passing by deletePageCompletelyBySystem, and the pre-existing backlog is the
admin page tree repair's to remove. A boot-time migration is the wrong place to
stall an upgrade on a collection-wide scan.

Because the sweep no longer runs first, "has descendants" is judged against the

instead of being granted an expiry. Nothing is deleted, but it stays WIP with no

The conversion also no longer materializes every legacy page. find().toArray()

fix(page): stop the empty-page sweep from stepping over live orphans

sweepAllEmptyLeaves advanced a $skip by the number of candidates the delete step
declined, to keep a fully declined batch from being re-offered forever. That
re-offer cannot happen: a declined candidate has either gained a child or stopped
being empty, which are exactly the two conditions the scan matches on, so it
drops out of the result set on its own. The scan is self-consuming and needs no
offset at all.

The offset therefore pointed past pages that were still orphans, stranding one
per decline — silently, showing up only as a lower `removed`. Removed, with the
reasoning recorded so it is not reintroduced.

MAX_BARREN_ROUNDS replaces it as the runaway guard, counted in rounds rather than
documents: a candidate spared by a child that is itself removed before the next
scan does legitimately come back, and bailing after two barren rounds caps that
without ever skipping a real candidate.

The new integration test narrows the real pipeline to one subtree with a batch of
2 and creates a child between the scan and the delete, since interleaving is the
only way to make the delete step decline. Re-adding the $skip fails it with one
stranded orphan; the other 11 tests in the file stay green, which is why it is
worth having.

Two causes. `actions/checkout` defaults to fetch-depth 1, so the base
branch's history is not in the checkout at all; and even with full history,
changesets runs `git merge-base master HEAD` with the bare name, which does
not resolve on a detached-HEAD checkout that only has remote-tracking refs.

Fetch the full history and pass the PR's own base explicitly. Using
`github.base_ref` rather than a hardcoded `master` keeps the check correct
for PRs targeting a release branch.

The workflow file is added to its own `paths:` so this change is exercised
by the PR that makes it, instead of merging unverified.

fix(i18n-key-audit): handle the 0-missing case in parseDefaultLanguageMissingCount

i18next-cli omits the "Primary language ... is missing N key(s)" line
entirely when that count is 0 -- exposed for the first time now that
task 7.3 brought en_US to 0 missing keys in the real repo.

Went through two rejected fixes before landing on a structural check:
anchoring on an unrelated header line let any wording change or
truncation silently return 0; a loose /missing/i keyword sniff still
missed rewordings that avoid that literal word. The final approach
extracts the stdout "slot" where the missing-line would appear (after
the last secondary-locale progress line) and requires it to be
genuinely blank before concluding 0 -- structural, not vocabulary-based.

One residual case is out of this module's boundary by design: a
capture truncated exactly at the start of that slot is textually
indistinguishable from a genuine zero-count ending there; detecting
that requires the caller to confirm the child process actually exited,
which this pure stdout-interpreting module does not do.

fix(i18n-key-audit): retry i18next-cli invocations on transient stdout truncation

The mergify merge-queue check for this PR (ci-app-lint run 32968568349,
PR #11795) failed lint:i18n with two different parse errors
(status --unused, status ko_KR). Reproduced locally: i18next-cli's
child-process stdout capture is intermittently truncated mid-output
(observed ~1 in 15-20 invocations) before it reaches the "Summary:"
line -- the captured text just stops partway through the list of
✓/✗ lines. This is an upstream stdout-flush race in the CLI's own
exit path, not a bug in Stdout Parser's regexes: fed the same
(genuinely truncated) string, they correctly throw rather than
guessing a count.

Add a bounded retry (3 attempts) around each measureCheck call in the
Audit Orchestrator, since a retry re-invokes the CLI for a fresh
capture rather than fabricating a result -- "a parse failure must
never be treated as 0/pass" still holds, since every attempt has to
fail for measureCheck to report an error. 12 consecutive stress-test
runs (7 + 5, two separate batches) show zero residual failures with
the fix; reproduced the original bug's absence of retry (a single
un-retried call) failing on the same fixture before the fix (RED),
and passing after (GREEN).

fix(test): cap integration test fork concurrency to stop migrate-mongo hook timeouts

test/setup/migrate-mongo.ts's beforeAll hook spawns a full `dev:migrate:up`
subprocess chain once per test file (VITEST_WORKER_ID, used to name each
file's database, is a per-file dispatch counter, not a bounded
physical-worker id). Without a concurrency cap, Vitest sizes its fork pool
off the CI runner's reported CPU count, and CI logs showed 100+ concurrent
migration attempts saturating the runner and blowing the hook's 20s budget.

Cap `test:integ`'s fork pool at 4 (matching GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest
runners) via --poolOptions.forks.maxForks, and add a modest 20s->30s
timeout margin on top as headroom, not a substitute for the cap. Local
reproduction (31-93 concurrent files) went from ~80% hook-timeout failures
to near zero after the cap.

    offset=5000  15,343 entries    9.9ms
    offset=100000 200,000 entries  78.0ms  returning nothing
    offset=999999999 200,000       76.8ms

perf(users): match username suggestions by collated prefix

The last unbounded cost in this lookup: a keyword with fewer matches than
`limit` could not stop early, so it walked the whole username index — and since
the cost is "how far to the 5th match", it grew as the keyword got more precise.
The expensive keystrokes were the useful ones. At 200k users, typing toward one
person: `ali` 471 entries / 0.9ms, `alic` 11,059 / 3.8ms, `alice` 200,001 /
57.5ms. After: 5 entries or fewer at every step, 1 for a no-match.

`$regex` is not collation-aware, so a case-insensitive pattern cannot be
index-bounded even when anchored — prefix matching alone would have changed
behaviour and bought nothing. The query is therefore a range compared under a
case-insensitive collation, against a new `username_ci` index. The unique
`username` index is untouched and still enforces uniqueness case-sensitively.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: matching is from the start of the username only. On this wiki
that is what people type (`kaho-y`, `kishimoto`, `mao-t` — the searchable part is
always at the front), which is also why a token index was rejected: its extra
findability would never be exercised here, at the cost of a derived field, a
backfill, a save hook and a gap on the data-import path.

`mixedUsernames` now merges results found by two rules (prefix for users,
substring for activity snapshots) — reason 3 of the July revert (c6d06a1f),
knowingly re-entered and pinned by an updated case rather than left implicit.

The upper bound is `prefix + U+FFFF`, not the last character incremented: ICU
sorts punctuation below letters, so `kahz` + 1 = `kah{` compares under `kahz`
and the range matches nothing. Verified against MongoDB — the increment form
returned 0 of the real matches for `kahz`, `zz` and `zzz`.

Mutation-checked: dropping `.collation()` fails the case-insensitivity case;
dropping the index declaration fails the cost guard (plan falls back to a
blocking SORT); the increment bound fails the high-letter case. The cost guard
asserts `totalDocsExamined`, not just keys — without a usable index the query
becomes a collection scan, where keysExamined is 0 and would pass a keys-only
check.

fix(page-view): stop remounting the page-body subtree on every re-render

PageView.tsx defined its page-body subtree as
`const Contents = useCallback(..., deps)` and rendered it as an
element type (`<Contents />`). useCallback returns a new function
identity whenever any dependency changes, and React treats a changed
element type as a different component, so the whole subtree was
unmounted and remounted on every dependency change -- including
SelectionCapture, whose lockedAnchor state (and any in-progress
InlineCommentForm) was silently reset to null.

This was pre-existing (same anti-pattern minus the inline-comment
deps), but was invisible until task 5.2 added
resolvedInlineCommentRanges to the dependency array --
useAnchorResolver returns a brand-new Map on every recomputation, so
this dependency's identity churns constantly, and SelectionCapture
now held state that mattered when reset. Found via task 6.2's E2E
test flaking at multiple unrelated interaction points.

Fix: useCallback -> useMemo, rendering the memoized value instead of
invoking it as a component type. Same dependencies, same body -- only
the render mechanism changes. Adds a permanent regression test to
PageView.spec.tsx proving SelectionCapture is never unmounted across
a page-body recompute.

fix(inline-comment): sort replies oldest-first to match normal comment thread order

InlineCommentService.listByPageId() queried replies with
createdAt: 'desc', matching only the raw fetch direction of the
normal-comment path's own query — but that path additionally reverses
the fetched comments client-side (PageComment.tsx's
commentsFromOldest) before grouping replies under their origin, so a
normal comment's reply thread always renders oldest-to-newest. Inline
comments had no equivalent reversal anywhere, so their replies
rendered newest-first, inconsistent with normal comments. Query
replies with 'asc' directly instead, since there is no client-side
reversal step for inline-comment replies to lean on.

fix(inline-comment): move reply oldest-first ordering to the client, not the API

The previous fix changed InlineCommentService.listByPageId()'s reply
query to createdAt: 'asc', but that conflated two different concerns:
the API's job is just to fetch in creation order, while display order
is the client's job — exactly how the page-footer comment API works

reverse it for display via commentsFromOldest). Revert the service
back to 'desc' for both origins and replies, and instead reverse
`replies` in InlineCommentReplies.tsx right before rendering, mirroring
PageComment.tsx's own reversal.

- Escape closed both the mention-picker dropdown (reactstrap's own
  handling) and the whole form in the same keypress, since reactstrap
  does not call preventDefault on Escape. The document-level Escape
  listener now runs in the capture phase and skips canceling while an

fix(inline-comment): raise the mention popup above the form and let clicks in it through

The mention-completion popup now floats outside InlineCommentForm (via
tooltips({parent: document.body}), previous commit), but it painted BEHIND
the form: SelectionPopover's portal sets an explicit z-index (1070,
Bootstrap's $zindex-popover), while the popup itself gets no z-index from
CodeMirror's base theme, so as a plain z-index:auto sibling it always
loses regardless of DOM order -- unreachable by the mouse.

Fixes it with a scoped EditorView.theme() extension raising
.cm-tooltip-autocomplete to z-index 1080 (Bootstrap's own $zindex-tooltip
tier). This uncovered a real bug in the shared appendExtensions utility
(packages/editor): EditorView.theme() returns an array of two extensions,
and passing that bare makes the utility split it across one shared
Compartment, throwing "Duplicate use of compartment in extensions" on
mount. Wrapping it in an extra array (`[tooltipZIndexTheme]`) keeps both
parts under one compartment slot, sidestepping the utility bug without
touching the shared package.

Moving the popup outside the form's own DOM subtree also broke the
form's outside-click-cancel handler: a click on a mention suggestion
looked like a click outside the form and canceled it before the
selection could land. handlePointerDown now recognizes
.cm-tooltip-autocomplete as part of the form for this purpose.

Verified against the real dev server: the popup no longer throws on
mount, elementFromPoint at a candidate's screen position resolves to the
candidate (not the form), and clicking a suggestion inserts it and keeps
the form open. Also: unit tests (27/27), typecheck, biome, and the full
inline-comment.spec.ts Playwright suite (55/55).

fix(inline-comment): keep list-click scroll navigation working for resolved comments

PageView.tsx excluded resolved comments from inlineCommentAnchors
entirely, so useAnchorResolver never computed a Range for them. This
correctly suppressed their passive highlight/popover (Requirement
2.7/4.1/4.3), but also broke scrollToRange: clicking a resolved
comment in the bottom list could no longer find its Range at all,
surfacing a misleading "could not be found... may have been edited or
removed" error for a comment whose text was untouched -- it was simply
resolved.

Anchors (and therefore resolvedInlineCommentRanges) are now computed
for ALL comments, resolved included, so scrollToRange (Requirement 16)
keeps working. A new derived visibleResolvedRanges filters OUT
resolved comments and is what InlineCommentHighlight and
InlineCommentBodyInteraction's hit-testing consume, so the passive
highlight/popover suppression is unaffected.

Reported by the user after the feature shipped; reproduced via a
Playwright test confirmed RED against the prior code (git stash) and
GREEN with this fix.

fix(editor): never publish a view-less editor as the first isolated-atom value

useCodeMirrorEditorIsolated's shouldUpdate skipped the isValid() check on a
hook instance's first publish attempt, so an editor whose CodeMirror
view/state hadn't finished async initialization could still be published
as the shared atom's first value. A one-shot initial-value applier (e.g.
MentionAwareCommentInput, used by the inline-comment edit modes) would
consume its single chance calling initDoc() against this no-op editor and
never retry once the atom was later updated with the real, valid one --
leaving the edit-mode input permanently empty in a real browser, even
though everything else about the editor worked correctly.

Fix: require isValid(newData) unconditionally, not just on later updates.
Verified via a throwaway real-browser reproduction (RED) and fix
confirmation (GREEN), plus a full pass of packages/editor's existing test
suite and an A/B check that the page-body editor's own e2e suite is
unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01STLAA61rVFKwknzMrg4ZTf

fix(editor): clear the isolated-editor atom when its publisher unmounts

Round-2 reviewer finding: the prior isValid() fix (40849cb3b7) closed the
first-open case, but the same atom is keyed per editorKey and was never
reset on unmount -- so re-opening edit mode on the same comment after
Cancel still showed an empty editor, because the second mount's first
render saw the atom still holding the PREVIOUS, destroyed editor and spent
MentionAwareCommentInput's one-shot initDoc call on it.

Resets the atom when the *publisher* (the hook instance that owns a
container, e.g. CodeMirrorEditor) unmounts, gated through a ref so a reader
-only consumer sharing the same key (MentionAwareCommentInput itself calls
this hook with no container) can never wipe a still-live editor.

Verified in a real browser: first open, re-open after cancel, and a third
open all now restore the original body; editing/saving still persists;
new-reply creation still works. New regression test (mutation-checked:
fails without the fix, passes with it) covers the remount scenario
directly.

fix(inline-comment): re-resolve highlight after a same-length text edit

observeContainerSettle observed its container with childList/attributes
only, omitting characterData. A same-length in-place text correction
(e.g. fixing a typo) makes React update an existing Text node's data
directly rather than adding/removing any element -- a characterData
MutationRecord, not childList -- so the observer never fired and
useAnchorResolver never re-matched the saved quote against the edited
text. A full page reload masked this (useAnchorResolver always resolves
once synchronously at mount, independent of this observer), which is
why the highlight came back on reload but not on returning from the
editor to View.

Confirmed via a live-page diagnostic that ReactMarkdown really emits a
standalone characterData record for this edit class, and via a minimal
happy-dom repro that a childList/attributes-only observer provably
misses it. Regression test added and mutation-checked.

fix(markdown): preserve inline style and class on rendered headings

Header (used for h1-h6 in the published-page renderer, apps/app/src/client/services/renderer/renderer.tsx
generateViewOptions) rebuilt its className from a fixed string and never
forwarded the react-markdown props for the original HTML attributes, so
a heading written as e.g. `<h2 style="color: #ff0000;" class="...">` lost
both its style and its class once the page was saved and viewed (the
editor preview uses no custom h1-h6 component, so it rendered correctly
there, masking the bug).

GROWI's sanitize schema (recommended-whitelist.ts) already allows
`style`/`class`/`className` on every element via the '*' attribute key,
so these attributes do reach Header - it was just dropping them.

Widen HeaderProps to JSX.IntrinsicElements['h1'] & { node }, spread the
unrecognized attributes onto CustomTag, and merge the user's className
with GROWI's own instead of overwriting it. Narrowed CustomTag's type to
the heading tag union (was `keyof JSX.IntrinsicElements`) since spreading
attrs needs a props shape assignable across the type, and headings are
the only tags Header is ever assigned to.

Added Header.spec.tsx (red before this fix, green after) asserting the
rendered DOM node keeps a user-supplied style and merges a user-supplied
class with GROWI's own.
